edition.alertText: Trump-Xi-Putin 80-min Shenzhen summit produces four-point 'peace declaration' — pledges stable energy flows, nuclear risk dialogue, ICC criticism, but NO mention of Iran or Ukraine wars; no concrete commitments; Trump says Iran must not get nuclear weapons; Houthi missile damages PIF sovereign wealth fund tower in Riyadh — Saudi Arabia's tallest skyscraper hit, material damage, no injuries; Trump tells Fox News Iran may be working on biological or chemical weapons — 'if it does happen, we wipe them out'; Bloomberg/NYT: new US strikes 'increasingly likely' — Netanyahu pushing for 4-to-7-day joint campaign; Trump has not decided; WSJ: VP Vance considering face-to-face talks with top Iranian security official — plans at preliminary stage; IRGC claims 2 more oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz on Thursday — adds to 3 claimed earlier same day; Saudi coalition intercepts 4 ballistic missiles in southern region + destroys missile launcher in Dhamar, Yemen; air raids on Sanaa; Pentagon: Iran war has cost US military more than $48B (up from $47.1B in October); IEA World Energy Outlook: Hormuz crisis is 'largest threat' to energy security in history; Iran rejects 'unconditional and unlimited' IAEA inspections while under attack — Isfahan enrichment plant uninspected; Orlen (Poland) becomes first buyer to terminate QatarEnergy LNG contract (1M tonnes/yr) since force majeure — observers warn more may follow; WHO: Yemen death toll since August escalation reaches 2,260 with 10,519 wounded; UNICEF: 330,000+ displaced including 174,000 children; oil drops — Brent ~$90.15 (-2.28%), WTI ~$82.55 (-2.37%) as summit fails to deliver Iran breakthrough; gold falls below $3,700 — 14-month low; EIA: US crude stocks draw 3.4M bbl (week ending Nov 14) — largest since September; OPEC November MOMR leaves 2026-2027 demand forecasts unchanged; OPEC+ meets Nov 29 on 2027 output expansion

situation: The much-anticipated Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen concluded on Thursday after approximately 80 minutes, producing a four-point 'peace declaration' that analysts described as 'heavier in symbolism than concrete breakthroughs.' The joint statement pledged stable energy flows and increased production of refined petroleum products, committed to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation, criticized the ICC for 'abusing its jurisdiction,' and expressed support for UN reform — but conspicuously omitted any mention of either the Iran or Ukraine wars. Trump told reporters the three leaders are 'making history' and said Xi agreed the Strait of Hormuz must remain open and Iran must not obtain nuclear weapons, though no mechanism to achieve either was announced. Xi urged the three powers to shed a 'Cold War mentality,' while Putin called the format 'useful.' The declaration's silence on Iran was particularly notable given that Trump had cited the conflict as a primary reason for the summit. In a separate Fox News interview, Trump said there are 'indications' Iran may be working on biological or chemical weapons, warning 'if it does happen, we wipe them out' — while also telling Israel's Channel 12 he is 'not rushing' and may wait until after the new year. Bloomberg and the New York Times reported that new US strikes are 'increasingly likely,' with Netanyahu reportedly pushing for a four-to-seven-day joint campaign, though Trump has not decided. The WSJ reported that VP Vance is considering face-to-face talks with a top Iranian security official, with plans described as being at a 'preliminary stage.' Iran's ambassador Reza Najafi told ISNA that Tehran will not accept 'unconditional and unlimited' IAEA inspections while under attack. The Pentagon confirmed the war has cost the US military more than $48 billion, up from $47.1 billion in mid-October.

Oil prices declined on Thursday and into Friday as the Shenzhen summit failed to produce any concrete breakthrough on Iran. Brent crude fell to approximately $90.15/bbl (-2.28%) and WTI dropped to approximately $82.55/bbl (-2.37%), with WTI steadying just above $82.50 on Friday morning — the lowest level in roughly four weeks. The IEA's World Energy Outlook called the Hormuz crisis the 'largest threat' to energy security in history, warning it could cut oil demand 4% by 2035 if sustained. The EIA reported a 3.4-million-barrel draw in US crude stocks for the week ending November 14 — the largest weekly draw since September — bringing total stocks to 424.2 million barrels, partially offsetting the bearish summit disappointment. OPEC's November Monthly Oil Market Report left 2026 and 2027 demand and supply forecasts unchanged, with OPEC+ scheduled to meet November 29 on 2027 output expansion plans. Gold fell below $3,700/oz for the first time since September 2025 — a 14-month low — as the strong US dollar (19-month high), expectations of a Fed rate hike in December (CME FedWatch odds near 90% for 25bp), and fading geopolitical risk premium continued to crush precious metals. Coal eased to approximately $143.50/tonne, retreating from multi-month highs as the broader commodity complex weakened. Poland's Orlen became the first buyer to terminate a QatarEnergy LNG contract (1 million tonnes/year) since the force majeure was declared in March, citing ongoing delivery failures — observers at S&P Global Platts and Oxford warned more buyer pullbacks may follow. The DES Northwest Europe LNG benchmark stood at $27.59/MMBtu on November 11, up 175% from a year earlier.

The IRGC claimed two more oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday — adding to the three tankers it claimed caught fire from mines earlier the same day — bringing the daily tally of claimed mine strikes to five, the highest single-day figure in weeks. CENTCOM and UKMTO have not independently confirmed these latest claims. The war-risk insurance cost per Hormuz transit remains at $64 million per tanker versus $54,000 pre-war. VLCC rates continued their steep decline: the MEG-China TD3C spot rate fell to approximately $1.06 million/day in Week 46, down 25.2% from the October 8 peak, while the US Gulf-China TD22 route plunged to approximately $232,000/day, down 63.6% from peak. In Yemen, Houthi forces launched missiles at Riyadh on Thursday, with one striking the Public Investment Fund (PIF) tower — Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund headquarters and the city's tallest skyscraper — causing material damage but no injuries. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted four ballistic missiles targeting the southern region, destroyed a missile launch platform in Yemen's Dhamar province, and carried out air raids on Sanaa. The WHO confirmed the death toll from the Yemen escalation since August has reached 2,260, with 10,519 wounded, and UNICEF said more than 330,000 people including 174,000 children have been displaced. Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council designated the Houthis a 'terrorist' organization on Thursday, with penalties up to execution for cooperation. Iraqi forces were reported set to deploy Friday into Jurf al-Sakhar, the Kataib Hezbollah stronghold south of Baghdad.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices eased from June-July peaks of $1,100-1,300/tonne to $740-890/tonne by mid-October (Kpler), but remain above pre-war avg of ~$500/tonne (CRU). ADNOC sees sulfur output doubling from 7M to 14-20M tonnes by 2030-2035 — CEO Al Jaberi calls sulfur 'the future gold' (Nov 18). ADNOC's Oct official selling price cut $70 to $890/tonne. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fifth consecutive month — September through mid-November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva at COP31 (Nov 14) warned 45 million people could face severe food insecurity — urged US and Iran to immediately allow ~5 fertilizer vessels/day through Hormuz within 7-10 days. Fertilizer prices up ~30% since blockades began (UN). WHO: Yemen death toll since August escalation reaches 2,260, with 10,519 wounded; UNICEF: 330,000+ displaced including 174,000 children. Sudan food prices doubled in 6 months; Nepal farmers cannot afford fertiliser. Countries facing significant impact: Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka. Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Poland's Orlen becomes first buyer to terminate QatarEnergy LNG contract (1M tonnes/yr, oil-linked, through 2034) citing ongoing force majeure — observers warn more pullbacks possible (S&P Global Platts, Nov 11). DES NW Europe LNG benchmark at $27.59/MMBtu on Nov 11, up 175% YoY. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85), down from 4-year high above €101/MWh prior week; EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). LNG crossings at Hormuz reached 32 in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year. IMF projects 2026 GDP contractions: Kuwait and Iraq ~16%, Qatar ~15%. LNG flows at 40-45% of prewar levels.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B. Allianz Trade estimates >$200B in physical damage across GCC — 80+ energy facilities struck, a third severely damaged; cumulative economic losses projected at $790B through 2030.

US midterm election day — polls open; US strikes IRGC ground control station on Qeshm Island — first attack since June; CENTCOM destroys 3 drones aimed at civilian mariners; Iran fires missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain — both intercepted; IRGC claims targeting US Fifth Fleet HQ and air base (denied by Pentagon); IRGC fires missiles at vessel Pania — claims engine room hit; US disables MT Lexi (Botswana-flagged tanker) with Hellfire missile for violating blockade; tanker struck by 2 projectiles off Oman — engine room damaged, no injuries; Indian-crewed dhow MSV Al Jusufi attacked — 1 Indian sailor killed, 13 rescued; IRGC claims 3 tankers hit mines transiting 'without permission'; IRGC claims 2 Lucas drones downed over Bandar Khamir; Rezaei: US response 'not convincing'; Qatar: feedback expected within 36 hours; Vance: hopeful for 'negotiated settlement'; Trump: deal 'could happen'; Pezeshkian: renewed fighting benefits 'no one'; Saudi coalition intercepts drone over Mecca + 2nd drone later; Houthis: Saudi strikes killed 17 over 2 days; Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B; Aramco begins 'preliminary' East-West pipeline expansion engineering; Iran executes 4 men including 2 for protests; Iran inflation at 88.7%; Kuwait activates air raid sirens nationwide; Bahrain activates warning sirens; Asian Cup postponed to Dec 2027; Brent partially recovers; oil rises on Qeshm strike

Democrats sweep US midterms — take House and Senate; Vance calls Iran war the 'obvious' reason for Republican rout; Trump says he'd 'do it again' and signals 'heavy hit' on Iran; oil crashes 9% — Brent plunges to $94.62 (-8.92%), WTI to $86.97 (-9.0%), biggest drop since July; Iran says Americans voted 'NO TO WAR' — Ghalibaf hails results; Mojtaba Khamenei warns of 'immediate' response if Trump resumes post-midterm strikes; Democrats demand end to war — plan to use Congressional majority to curb Trump's war powers; IRGC claims strikes on multiple tankers 'emboldened' after elections — says four tankers destroyed by mines, two detained; Iranian general warns of Red Sea attacks if fighting resumes; VLCC rates plunge $100K+ on peace hopes; gold slips to $3,912; coal eases to $146.20; US gasoline $4.13/gal (AAA); ~2/3 of Americans disapprove of Trump's Iran war handling (Pew); war cost estimated at $2,000/household (Moody's); Houthis claim missile attack on Saudi city; Saudi coalition strikes Hodeidah; Hormuz flows ~11.7M b/d in Oct (Breakwave); ~80 VLCCs in Gulf-Oman shuttle ops; Qatar draft proposal still under review; fertilizer shipments through Hormuz zero for 4th month

Four explosions rock Qeshm Island — IRNA reports impacts at Suza, cause unknown; additional blasts at Sirik, Jask, Bandar Abbas; IRGC claims 3 tankers caught fire in Hormuz on 'unauthorized' route — Fars: 2 hit mines, 1 exploded; Iranian navy says tanker hit mine east of strait; bulk carrier incident 18nm east of Khor Fakkan; UAE National Guard rescues 22 from cargo ship fire in Sea of Oman; Houthi cruise missiles damage KAFD tower in Riyadh (Reuters) + Aramco building (minor damage); Saudi coalition intercepts 2 cruise missiles over Riyadh + Houthi drone in eastern region; coalition destroys missile launchers and launch platform in Sanaa; IRGC dismisses Task Force Iron Gate as 'wordplay'; Araghchi: no negotiations since midterm 'shock'; Iran armed forces: US midterm defeat reflects failure; Israel defense minister Katz: 'mission not complete'; Trump tells CNN strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress; Iran executes 3 men over 2026 protests; IRGC lifts self-imposed 2,000km missile range cap per Khamenei directive
